brief: Makes and checks RFC 6238 time-based one-time passwords, the second factor of an authenticator app, with the hashing done in the engine.
detail: The shared secret is base32, the text a user types into an app; the class decodes it to hex for the engine call, so no raw key bytes cross the text boundary. The defaults, SHA1, 6 digits and a 30-second step, are what Google Authenticator, Authy, 1Password and FreeOTP expect. Verify tolerates a small clock drift, and compares in constant time. A code is not consumed by a check: the same code verifies again within its window, so the caller must remember the last step it accepted to refuse a reuse. The secret itself is shown by Show and Secret and carried in the provisioning address, so treat all three as sensitive. The examples use the public RFC 6238 test secret.
